fatal_errors: The proposed 0.5 at.% W addition does not reconstruct the target intervention, which varied Mo content from x = 0.2 to 0.5 and 1 in a CoCrFeNiMox-Ni/MoS2-Ag-Cr2O3 composite.
The starting material is misidentified as undoped, single-phase CoCrFeNi rather than the SPS-fabricated multicomponent self-lubricating composite used as the target baseline.
Evidence E2 concerns an AlCoCrFeNiWx coating tested at high temperature and cannot substantiate consistent performance of bulk CoCrFeNi-W from room temperature to 800 °C, especially in vacuum.
The claim of a continuous low-shear W-derived tribofilm across the entire temperature range is unsupported; W-rich hard particles and oxides are not established as room-temperature lubricants.
The predicted coefficient of friction of 0.2–0.3 and order-of-magnitude wear reduction throughout the full range are substantially stronger than the cited evidence permits.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the broad challenge and gives one testable compositional intervention, but it is not a reconstruction of the target study. The target relies on increasing Mo in a composite already containing Ni/MoS2, Ag, and Cr2O3. Its wide-temperature behavior results from different mechanisms in different regimes: MoS2 and Ag at low-to-medium temperature, Mo-induced lattice distortion and sigma-phase strengthening, and compacted NiO/silver-molybdate glaze formation at 600–800 °C. The generated hypothesis instead extrapolates a W effect observed in an Al-containing HEA coating at 800 °C to a different alloy form, composition, full temperature interval, multiple loads, and both air and vacuum. The proposed experiment includes an appropriate control and useful friction, wear, and microscopy measurements, but lacks fixed loads, speeds, distances, counterface, replication, and statistical criteria. Its falsification rule is also overly demanding because failure at any single condition across a broad factorial test would reject the entire hypothesis. E1 and E3 provide little relevant tribological support, while E2 supports only the narrower proposition that 0.5 at.% W can improve high-temperature wear in a related AlCoCrFeNi coating.
